title: 360° MDL: A Multi-Stream, Multidimensional and Resilience-Tested Methodology for Literature Reviews—Design, Open Toolkit and Demonstration in Two Applied Reviews
content: Literature reviews are among the most read and cited scholarly publications, yet most draw on one or two databases, privilege the most-cited voices and report conclusions without testing whether they depend on the choice of sources. Reporting guidelines secure transparency of searching and selection but do not prescribe how to balance academic, practice, policy and emerging evidence, or how to measure the robustness of conclusions. We present 360° MDL, the Multidimensional Literature Review Model, developed with a design-science approach and released with an open toolkit and a 30-item reporting checklist. It combines five evidence stream families, a three-gate selection process with a six-criterion quality gate and portfolio rules, eight analysis matrices, and indices of stream balance, coverage, method diversity and resilience; each key finding is graded by its Triangulation Strength across stream families and stress-tested by leaving one family out. Two applied reviews, in clinical artificial intelligence and in genetic cardiomyopathy, demonstrate it: non-database streams supplied 60–64% of the core corpora, most key findings were robust across three or more families, and a database-only design would have missed two to three findings per review. 360° MDL complements PRISMA and offers authors, editors and assessors an auditable route from evidence volume to tested synthesis.
